# FIRST HALF – The claim and its reproduction {#first-half-the-claim-and-its-reproduction .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
First half
:::

::: notes
The first half. I start with the vocabulary of three kinds of repetition, from the glossary that the SCORE programme published, and with the Multi100 project from the inside, because I was one of the five analysts who reanalysed the claim that we work on. Then the paper itself: the survey question behind it, the scales, the panel that you have in your browser, the model and the claim, and what SCORE found when it tried to reproduce and to replicate the study. You write the question that the claim answers, in one sentence, and we read the class at once. And before the break you reproduce the result that one of two analysts recorded, to the third decimal, and find out why your number is exactly that number and why the other group has another one.
:::

# SECOND HALF – The multiverse of the claim {#second-half-the-multiverse-of-the-claim .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Second half
:::

::: notes
Welcome back. In the first half you reproduced a recorded number. Now you become the sixth analyst and make choices of your own. I open the menu of the fourteen decisions that any analysis of this claim has to take, with the survey decisions first, because this audience knows that part of the menu best, and show you the code behind the menu. Then you work the menu in the browser lab, one decision at a time, and send the analysis that you would defend to the class chart. We read the class against the curve of every justifiable analysis of these data, ask which decision moves the estimates most, and what such a curve can and cannot establish. We end with the critics, with what a preregistration would have added, and with the replication of this claim on new data.
:::
